comment: The table of the cache of the library builds: the lookup, the store and the stats line in
src/fort/library/cache.ft, the manifest, the reader and the writer of the entry of an entry
unit and the source hash of a walk in src/fort/library/artifact.ft, and the options, the
builds that use the cache, the hits and the stores in src/fort/driver.ft (D9.11,
toolchain.md 1, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3). Each row breaks one rule. The module suites compile the
mutated module themselves; the build links the compiler so that the md5 guard reads it, and
the last stage runs test/library/cache_test.py over that compiler. The table runs in the VM
with the default runner after `tools/vm configure` and `tools/vm build`. The build waits 2 s
and touches the sources in the guest first, as tools/mutations/use_fort.json does. The rule
that a hit of the entry unit checks nothing more has no row: a check that runs anyway writes
the same output, so only the time of the build shows it. The guard `libs.len > 0`
of a build with --use has no row either: without it a whole program looks its key up and
stores nothing, and no build stores an entry under that key (its compiler field is empty),
so the lookup is always a miss that writes nothing (driver_cache_test,
a_whole_program_touches_no_cache, holds that no cache directory appears).
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/library/cache.ft src/fort/library/artifact.ft src/fort/driver.ft && cmake --build build/Linux/debug --target fort

stages.name: the module suites of the cache
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std library/cache library/artifact_entry library/artifact_reading library/artifact_test driver_cache driver_use driver_test driver_artifact

stages.name: the cache with the real tools
stages.command: python3 test/library/cache_test.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu

mutations.what: an entry whose key line holds another key hits
a missing entry reads as corrupt
the lookup follows a link at the entry
a cache directory that is a file reads as a corrupt entry
an entry that cannot be read reads as corrupt
the lookup reads every entry as a library entry
the store writes through a link at the layout directory
mutations.old: return make_dir(dir, true) && make_dir(layout, false) && make_dir(entry, false);
mutations.new: return make_dir(dir, true) && make_dir(layout, true) && make_dir(entry, true);

mutations.what: the stats line of a miss gives no cause
the stats line writes the name with no escape
the manifest of an entry unit writes the archiver
the manifest of an entry unit writes the outputs of a library
an object that differs from its hash is read
the object line is no hash field
the source hash of a walk hashes the first file for each module
the writer of an entry unit keeps the old manifest
--cache-stats needs no library build
--cache-stats reports before --cache-dir
the build ignores --cache-dir
a --lib build with -c uses the cache
the default cache of --lib is in the current directory
a hit of a library builds it again
a library build stores no entry
a library build whose tool failed writes the stats line
a build with --fir-stats uses the cache
the default cache of an entry unit is in the current directory
a build with --use stores no entry
a hit of the entry unit writes no object
the entry line names the file and not the module
the archiver runs with the environment of the compiler
the check of the layout refuses a link at `1`, so a file at the entry behind it reads as unreadable
under -c a miss writes the hit object, an empty one, to the -c output
the store reads the object back from the -c output
a -c output gets 0644 and not 0666 less the umask
a regular -c output is written in place
a FIFO or a device at the -c output is replaced by a rename
an absent -c output is written in place
a link at the -c output is written through and not replaced
a -c output whose temporary file cannot be made is no write
